_comment: LOW-THRESHOLD NIGHTLY ALERT STREAM op-point -- the ~10k/night ranked QA product, NOT the science alert op. The frozen science product stays op_2v_alert.json (score 0.80/mfsnr 5/chi2 5) and is produced by a separate, unchanged linking pass in the same run_night chain; this one deliberately trades purity for volume so a night can be eyeballed for systematics and the cut chosen LATER, downstream, on the ranked list (Mario, 2026-07-26: 'go with the lower threshold, we can make a cut wherever we think we need to').
_scope: NEO-focused: the 1-8 deg/day same-night rate band is KEPT (it is the physics scope of the 2-visit product, and the seeder+chi2 are calibrated inside it). Faster impactor-like rates (>8 deg/day) are OUT of this stream by construction -- widening the band is a separate, measured change (the seeder caps at rate_max 10).
_volume: Volume is NOT set by these gates. They are deliberately loose; the nightly count is fixed by taking the top --stream-top-n RANKED alerts for imaging (run_night default 10000), so the stream is the same size on a sparse night and a dense one. Measured on real night 20260630 (27 visits, 387,826 dets at score>=0.5): chi2<=5 -> 938 alerts, chi2<=15 -> 6,239. NOTE the count at a given chi2 must be MEASURED by running at that gate: chi2_2v_max also feeds the partial-chi2 prefilter and the pair dedup, so a looser run's chi2 distribution does NOT predict a tighter run's count (chi2<=5 subset of the chi2<=15 run = 645, vs 938 when actually run at 5).
_ranking: Alerts are ranked by the standard rank_alerts ordering (demotion class, then priorityScore = tier base + 0.95*weakest-member CNN score + dt bonus), so vetoed alerts sort last and the frozen science alerts keep their relative order. At stream volume this is dominated by the CNN score; a chi2/mfsnr-aware CALIBRATED reality probability is the intended upgrade.
